fn.en: Say what you can and can’t do.
fn.ru: Говорить, что ты умеешь и что не умеешь.
fn.kk: Не істей алатыныңды және алмайтыныңды айту.

can.en: I can say what I can and can’t do.
can.ru: Я могу сказать, что я умею и что не умею.
can.kk: Не істей алатынымды және алмайтынымды айта аламын.

tip.en: can + verb, no -s and no to: She can swim.
tip.ru: can + глагол, без -s и без to: She can swim.
tip.kk: can + етістік, -s те, to да жоқ: She can swim.

items.why: can never takes -s: he can, she can.

items.q: I can swim, but I ___ swim often.
items.why: ability = can; how often = Present Simple.

items.a: My brother can play the guitar
I can cook but I don’t cook often

items.s: She ___ drive — she hasn’t got a licence. 🚫
I sing very ___ — nobody wants to listen! 👎
Typing fast is a useful ___ at work. 🛠

lines: “[Can|Do|Are] you swim?” — “Yes, I [can|can swim to|do]. I can swim [well|good|well good].”
“And [are|can|do] you good with a computer?” — “I type quite slowly, but I [can|can to|cans] use different programs.”
“[Can|Do|Does] you drive?” — “No, I [can’t|don’t can|can’t to]. But I can learn.”
My colleague [can|cans|can to] speak four languages. She [can’t|doesn’t can|not can] drive.
I can cook, but I [don’t|can’t|doesn’t] cook often — I haven’t got time.

tts: My neighbours have a parrot, Murphy. He’s an amazing bird! Murphy can sing and speak, too. He likes dancing and he can listen to The Beatles for hours. There are two songs Murphy loves, but he hates one of them — nobody knows why!

acts.title: The interview
text: I’m Jack and this is my job interview. 💼
“Can you swim?” — “Yes, I can. I can swim well.” 🏊
“Can you use a computer?” — “I type quite slowly, but I can use different programs.” ⌨️
“Can you drive?” — “No, I can’t. But I can learn — I’m a fast learner.” 🚗🚫
“Can you use a camera?” — “Yes, I can. I like photography a lot.” 📷

items.s: Jack can use different computer programs.

items.sit: At a job interview you are asked: “Can you swim?” You swim well.
o: Yes, I can. I can swim well.
Yes, I can to swim well.
Yes, I do. I swim good.

You talk about your brother. He plays the guitar.

o: I can to speak three languages.

items.sit: You know how to cook, but you order food most evenings.
o: I can cook, but I don’t cook often.
I can cook, but I can’t cook often.
I cook can, but not often.

items.sit: You want to know if your new colleague types fast.

lines.s: I haven’t got time. I ___ get home before eight.
Then he can play and you can ___!

write.q: Write 6 sentences: three things you can do, two you can’t do, and one you can do but don’t do often.
write.model: I can swim and I can drive. I can speak three languages. I can’t sing — I sing very badly. I can’t play the guitar. I can cook, but I don’t cook often, because I get home late.

speak.q: Answer out loud: Can you swim? Can you drive? Can you play an instrument? Then ask two Can you…? questions.
speak.model: Yes, I can. I can swim well. No, I can’t drive. I can play the guitar, but I don’t play often. Can you cook? Can you type fast?

items.l: What time do you get up? ⏰
How often do you study English? 🔁
Does your sister work at night? 🌙
Why do you get up at five? 💭
items.r: Because I start work at seven.
